At stake is the lust for power over man, best exemplified by Zerahemnah, Amalickiah, and Ammaron, in opposition to reliance on God's power, demonstrated by Moroni and Helaman. Moroni's courageous assertion, "Ye cannot destroy this our faith" (Alma 44:3), shows his confidence in the Book of Mormon promiseregarding the rewards of keeping God's commandments.

Only in one case is there description of a "sword" with any kind of point: a Nephite soldier "smote" a Lamanite leader, accidentally scalping him; then he carefully picked up the scalp, "laid it" on the "point" of his sword (rather than spearing it, as we might expect), and raised it aloft (Alma 44:12-13). This odd description fails to make clear exactly how the weapon looked.
